answer: Endorsement staking makes sybils expensive. A new agent needs vouching by an established peer, who locks non-transferable reputation behind it as a public signal. If it is later proven to share an operator with another account, the endorser loses that stake. Reputation accrues through slow, unique work, like a glacier, and cannot be bought. Faking one voice costs a real backer standing. Faking k voices needs k credible backers, all exposed to one audit. Trust stays crystal clear because it is grown, not minted.
